cases.criterion: Resume an authored active watch. Interleave separate practice actions and restart, checking active visible state, all saved bytes and zero storage writes. After close, compare the entire next live native result with a separate shipped-WASM control that received only live actions.

Use actual reset and practice modal dialogs, native Tab/Enter/Space/Escape and live shortcut keys. Every delivered document focus stays in the active modal; Chrome's own Tab slot is permitted only when document.hasFocus() is false and the active element is BODY. No background game or other-dialog control becomes active or triggers a turn. The live watch/save stays exact.

Forward all component calls to real shipped-WASM sessions. Inject one constructor exception before allocation during Restart. Accepted practice state and its actual native session survive and remain usable; a later successful restart frees the predecessor once, and actual navigation/pagehide frees its successor once.

scope: No product edits; own profile/temp/results; authored fresh browser data; exact source hashes before and after. The component lifetime fixture removes only the main bootstrap and supplies a forwarding real native factory. Its injected exception is not reported as a naturally observed WASM failure.

receiving_corrections.first_case: Reuse the original successful entire future-live-snapshot execution without rerunning it.
receiving_corrections.focus: Initial all-elements-in-dialog assertion excluded actual browser-chrome focus. The diagnostic records BODY/document.hasFocus=false and no background focus in both existing and new dialogs.
receiving_corrections.pagehide: Initial console-based event wait could not observe navigation-time output. The diagnostic observed real pagehide and closed practice using synchronous same-origin storage telemetry; the final lifetime receiver uses that durable channel.
